correctness.rationale: The degree-q+1 vanishing forms are the alternating Frobenius forms, by projective reduction of x_i^q x_j followed by interpolation, valid also in characteristic two. Alternating congruence gives the normal form, a smooth base on 2r variables and k free coordinates; over a field of size Q these multiply the base count by Q^k and add the vertex. I checked the all-extension formula independently by additive characters. For Q=q^s and nonzero character parameter a, summing a single alternating pair over y leaves Q times the indicator of a^q x^(q²)=a x. By cyclicity of the multiplicative group, for odd s there are q solutions x for every a; for even s there are q² on the subgroup a^((Q−1)/(q+1))=1 and one otherwise. Multiplying over the r pairs and projectivizing yields the primitive correction Q^(r−1) times q^r for odd s and (q^(2r)+q)/(q+1) for even s. Its formal exponential splits into the two claimed signs with the announced multiplicities; the k unused coordinates yield the shifts and vertex factors. This also covers r=1 (q+1 separate base-field points) and k=0. The q² excess over the ambient hyperplane count has one strictly rank-decreasing term, and congruence identifies the corresponding projective class. The frozen purity argument is consistent with this derivation; the two signs are characteristic-polynomial multiplicities, not an assertion of semisimplicity.
residual_risks: The frozen spot checks use q=2,3,5, even coordinate counts and extension degree at most four; the all-prime-power and all-dimension justification comes from proof, not those checks.

originality.rationale: Only the uniform full base-field Frobenius spectrum across all alternating ranks is credited as the distinct contribution. The normal form and smooth subclass are known; the quadratic count and its rank-separation interpretation follow from the classical degenerate Hermitian formula and alternating congruence. A quadratic spectrum alone loses signs under squaring; recovering the base-field characteristic polynomial and extending across all cones uses the space-filling trace in addition to those prior results. No inspected separate statement gives that all-rank, all-extension formula.
residual_risks: Bounded inspection is not historical priority certification. Older accounts formulated as Hermitian descents or parity-dependent counts could overlap with the full spectrum.
Same-day index dates give no within-day priority.

value.rationale: Computing the complete arithmetic invariant of the entire natural minimum-degree family is meaningful when every base-field rational point set is identical, and when the Hermitian model over the quadratic field hides the odd-extension behavior. The formula uniformly includes all singular ranks and gives a concrete, readily usable distinction between their projective classes. The value is in the full descent spectrum, not the routine quadratic monotonicity corollary alone.
residual_risks: No claims beyond ordinary zeta functions at the minimum space-filling degree.
